title: SparkBuild: Ignite your next tech project
summary: Turns a hardware idea into a cited, sourced, 3D build plan.
description: SparkBuild turns a plain-language hardware idea into a complete, cited build plan — research, a sourced bill of materials, and a self-paced build lesson — so anyone curious about hardware can get past "I don't know where to start." A research agent returns a typed, cited proposal from your goal and constraints (budget, parts owned, experience level), while a security and relevance agent rejects off-topic or malicious requests up front. A ranked bill of materials maps every part to a real catalog entry with an image and shop link, preferring parts you already own, and a freely navigable Workshop walks each cited step with a clear completion condition, an inline skills library, a 3D guide, and a circuit diagram. The assembly is an interactive React/Three.js view where the LLM only makes schema-validated symbolic choices and a deterministic solver owns all spatial math, so parts and coordinates are never fabricated. It runs local-first: a deterministic fixture mode delivers the full idea-to-lesson flow with no Docker, GPU, or cloud, while the local stack adds pgvector retrieval, inventory, and background n8n ingestion behind a single allowlisted upsert endpoint — learner requests never leave the machine.
descriptionShort: SparkBuild turns a plain-language hardware idea into a complete, cited build plan — research, a sourced bill of materials, and a self-paced 3D build lesson — so anyone curious about hardware can get past "I don't know where to start."
bullets: Built a local-first TypeScript monorepo (SparkBuild) that turns a plain-language hardware idea into a typed, cited plan across a four-tab Workshop: research, a sourced bill of materials, a self-paced lesson, and an interactive 3D assembly.

Enforced build accuracy by Zod-validating every cross-package boundary and letting the LLM make only symbolic, schema-validated choices while a deterministic solver owns all spatial transforms — no fabricated parts or coordinates.
Shipped a demo-safe deterministic fixture mode needing no cloud or GPU, then scaled to private on-device inference (Ollama) with PostgreSQL/pgvector retrieval and allowlisted n8n ingestion.

title: AGAT: Affordable General Aviation TCAS
summary: Collision avoidance for small aircraft at 0.5% the cost.
description: Built in under 48 hours at the DevilsInvent: Future-Ready Avionics hackathon (sponsored by Honeywell Aerospace), AGAT brings TCAS-style collision avoidance to general aviation, where commercial systems cost $200,000+ and price out small pilots. The concept listens to existing ADS-B broadcasts and a peer-to-peer LoRa link to map nearby aircraft and predict collisions, then integrates with the autopilot to automatically fly coordinated avoidance maneuvers — all from ~$900 of off-the-shelf parts (~$5,000 installed, roughly 0.5% of a commercial unit). The working prototype demonstrates the full pipeline with two ESP32 boards: each measures the gap with an ultrasonic sensor and relays alerts over ESP-NOW, while a Node.js server fuses the readings through a Kalman filter and TCAS II v7.1 threat logic, driving dual TCAS traffic displays (one per aircraft POV) and a 3D traffic view.
bullets: Built AGAT, a peer-to-peer collision-avoidance system for general aviation, in under 48 hours at the DevilsInvent x Honeywell hackathon — delivering TCAS-style protection at ~$5,000 installed, roughly 0.5% of a commercial system's $200,000+ cost.

Engineered a real-time prototype of two ESP32 boards streaming ultrasonic range over WebSockets and ESP-NOW into a Node.js Kalman filter and TCAS II v7.1 threat logic, rendered as dual TCAS displays and a 3D traffic view.
Designed automatic avoidance around existing ADS-B and autopilot systems to execute coordinated climb/descend maneuvers the moment a collision became imminent.
